text:
ConocoPhillips fell a modest 0.43% today to close at $141.73, capping a strong two-week rally of 11.55%. The small decline came despite oil prices remaining elevated—US crude at $101.91 per barrel—likely because the stock had run up sharply over the prior two trading days (up nearly $5 from October 13 to October 14) on Middle East supply concerns, and traders may have taken some profits after that quick advance.

The broader backdrop remains supportive for oil refiners and producers. Ongoing Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and a container ship sinking have kept geopolitical risk premiums baked into prices, while the IEA's planned diesel release signals concern about tight supply. However, today's modest pullback suggests the initial shock from escalating Middle East tensions has been partially digested by the market.
